title: Analog In-Memory Computing Enhanced FPGA for High-Throughput and Energy-Efficient Acceleration
problem: FPGA routing fabric incurs high data movement overhead because large amounts of data must be shuttled between compute and memory blocks, limiting energy efficiency for AI workloads.
motivation: The growing demand for AI computing coupled with slowing chip manufacturing performance gains makes energy-efficient FPGA-based accelerators increasingly critical.
method: The paper enhances FPGAs with in-memory computing macros based on non-volatile RRAM devices, specifically analog Dot Product Engines. Using the Verilog to Routing (VTR) framework, they simulate a novel 40 nm architecture and employ a custom event-driven simulator to evaluate performance.
key_novelty: Integration of analog RRAM-based Dot Product Engines directly into FPGA fabric to eliminate data movement overhead through in-memory computing.
contributions: Novel FPGA architecture enhanced with analog in-memory computing macros using RRAM devices
Design and simulation methodology for FPGA-integrated analog Dot Product Engines at 40 nm
Demonstration of 31.4× average throughput improvement over state-of-the-art FPGA implementations
Achievement of 9,380× energy efficiency improvement and 25.5×10³ TOPS/W performance
baselines: state-of-the-art FPGA implementations of AI models
